stories.headline: Poilievre defends leadership at Canada Strong and Free Network conference amid Conservative turmoil
stories.summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre delivered his keynote at the annual Canada Strong and Free Network conference in Ottawa on May 7, pledging to 'keep fighting' against what he called a 'club of Liberal elites,' while analysts and commentators noted a subdued crowd and ongoing internal pressure after floor-crossings helped Carney secure a majority. Multiple French and English outlets covered the speech, party strategy questions, and Poilievre's poll deficit.

Smith said she left more confident but no final agreement was announced; Carney also raised concerns about the leak of Alberta voter data during the meeting.

stories.headline: Carney addresses trade, US integration, and global partnerships at Toronto summit; Obama visit triggers MAGA backlash
stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney closed the 2026 Global Progress Action Summit in Toronto on May 9, signalling openness to deeper US integration in some sectors ahead of the CUSMA review while also pushing for trade diversification. Former US President Obama attended the summit, prompting criticism from US conservatives who alleged a 'Logan Act violation,' which fact-checkers dismissed. Carney also met with Bay Street financial CEOs in Toronto on the same trip.

Prime Minister Carney invoked the Clarity Act and vowed to make the federation work for Alberta, while a senior UCP staffer was found to have attended a Centurion Project demonstration that exposed millions of Albertans' personal data.

stories.headline: CSIS 2025 annual report released; India rejects espionage allegations, Khalistan extremism cited as threat
stories.summary: The Canadian Security Intelligence Service's 2025 public report, tabled in Parliament on May 2, identified China, Russia, India, Iran and Pakistan as key foreign interference actors while also flagging Canada-based Khalistani extremist groups as a national security threat. India's foreign ministry flatly rejected the espionage allegations as 'baseless' while pointing to Canada's failure to act on Khalistan-linked violence.

stories.headline: Carney names former Supreme Court justice Louise Arbour as next Governor General
stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney announced on May 6 that Louise Arbour, a former Supreme Court justice and international human rights prosecutor, will become Canada's next governor general, succeeding Mary Simon. The appointment was approved by King Charles. Quebec sovereigntist parties questioned the relevance of the position while English Canada broadly praised Arbour's credentials.

stories.headline: Canada's April unemployment rises to 6.9% as economy sheds 17,700 jobs, complicating Bank of Canada outlook
stories.summary: Statistics Canada data released May 8 showed the unemployment rate rose to a six-month high of 6.9% in April as the economy shed 17,700 jobs, well below expectations. The Bank of Canada, which held rates at 2.25% for a fourth consecutive time in late April, now faces tension between a softening labour market and inflation risks from energy prices, with economists divided on whether the next move will be a cut or hold.

Erskine-Smith did not concede immediately, alleging irregularities in the process.

stories.headline: Ontario Liberal leadership race heats up as MPP Lee Fairclough enters contest
stories.summary: Ontario Liberal MPP Lee Fairclough announced her bid for the provincial party's leadership on May 8, joining a growing field that includes Nate Erskine-Smith, MPP Rob Cerjanec, and others. The leadership vote is scheduled for November, with the party seeking to rebuild after three consecutive provincial election losses.

stories.headline: BC Conservative leadership race reaches final debate as party holds commanding poll lead over NDP
stories.summary: Five candidates vying to lead the BC Conservative Party held their final leadership debate on May 10, with ballots already distributed to over 42,000 members ahead of a May 30 convention. Polls show the leaderless BC Conservatives holding a 10-point lead over Premier David Eby's NDP, driven by dissatisfaction over Indigenous land title policy and affordability.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney confirmed he will use the independent advisory body for Senate appointments 'in due course' while a senior government official confirmed senators will not be allowed back into the Liberal caucus, ending speculation about reversing the Trudeau-era expulsion.
